content.text:
The whole plan is implemented and verified on branch `claude/language-capability-generalization` (3 commits, stacked on the parameter-names branch). Everything is committed locally; I have **not** pushed or opened a PR.

## What shipped

**P0 — advertising.** `CONSTRUCTS` now declared wherever `CALLS` is (it's relabelled off the same pass); Julia and R added to `supportsCallExtraction`. The new contract test then caught a third case I'd missed — Rust emits `OVERRIDES` for trait impls and didn't declare it.

**P0 — contract test.** `TestCapabilityMatrixCoversEmittedRelations` asserts every relation a fixture emits is declared per-language or as a global heuristic, one direction only (per Codex's caveat: a fixture lacking a construct isn't evidence of missing capability).

**P1a — fast profile.** The gate is now opt-out keyed on semantic support instead of a 17-language allowlist.

**P1b — AST types.** Return/param types come from the parse tree, with the signature-string split as fallback. Plumbed through `Entity` → `SymbolRecord` → search cache as private fields (schema 1.x untouched).

**P2 — registries + docs.** `importsFor` and `importCapableExtension` now read one registry (which also hoists per-file regex compilation to package scope); `docs/baseline-report.md` corrected, with a test pinning it to the executable list.

**Plus two things the work turned up.** The GraphQL body scan ran on every language with a case-insensitive `(query|mutation|subscription) <word>` pattern — 1,245 junk edges in cli-cli and 1,057 in spring, targeting things like `query the`. It's now restricted to the languages that declare `HANDLES_GRAPHQL`. And I widened fixture coverage from 11 to 21 languages, which surfaced 25 more undeclared relations across C, C++, Groovy, Julia, Kotlin, Ruby, Scala, Swift, Zig — all now declared.

## Verification

| check | result |
|---|---|
| P0 + P2 output impact | **byte-identical** across all 12 corpus/profile snapshots |
| full suite / gofmt / vet | green |
| snapshot determinism | 5 runs, one hash |
| cached vs cold `--head` | identical content |
| fast CALLS ⊆ full CALLS | **0** spurious edges across 4 repos |

Aggregate relation deltas: `full` — RETURNS_TYPE **+2,893**, HANDLES_GRAPHQL **−2,327**, PARAM_TYPE **−1,403**, CALLS +150. `fast` — CALLS **+10,539**, CONSTRUCTS +381.

I opened every category of removal against source. All correct: `PARAM_TYPE` losses were parameter *names* (`args`, `run`) and receivers; `RETURNS_TYPE` losses were parameter types or the method's own name (`Register -> CommandCallback` on a method that returns nothing; `load_host_triple -> GlobalContext`, a param). Gains verified too — Zig's `reclaim_table(...) ?*RepairTable` now correctly yields `RepairTable`.

## Two things you should weigh

**The fast profile got slower** where it now does work it previously skipped (median of 3, post-warmup): cargo 4.27→10.41s, pandas 41.99→71.34s, spring 26.86→30.79s, cli-cli 10.98→9.32s. Cargo at `fast` is still 3.6× faster than at `full` (37.85s) while going from 14 CALLS to 8,914. I judged that worth it — the old behavior wasn't fast, it was empty — but it's a real cost and reversible if you disagree.

**The GraphQL gate is incomplete.** It aligns emission with declared capability, but the regex is still loose *within* the declaring languages: pandas retains 88 edges named `query the`, `query is`, `query that`. Tightening the pattern is a precision fix outside this plan's scope — say the word and I'll do it or file it.

Also noted, not touched: a pre-existing `self-assignment of i to i` vet warning in `internal/cli/search.go:1193` from `bd325aa` on the base branch.

Want me to push this branch and open a draft PR stacked on #75?

cd /Users/thomi/Projects/entire-graph; gh pr create --draft --base claude/tree-sitter-parameter-names --head claude/language-capability-generalization --title "graph: derive language capability from behavior, not hand-kept lists" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
Stacked on #75 (base: `claude/tree-sitter-parameter-names`). Draft.

Third in the chain from the determinism report in #73. #75 fixed one instance of a defect class; this fixes the class wherever it appears, and adds the guards that make it stay fixed.

**The class:** a capability is gated on a hand-maintained per-language list while the real behavior is generic, so the two drift — and a language silently gets a worse path, or a promise the provider does not keep.

The codebase already had the right pattern in the same file: `supportsSemanticExtraction` derives from `spec.grammar != nil`, and `importCapable` derives from a shared predicate. `supportsCallExtraction` (a 30-language switch) and `ooRelationSupport` (a hand table) did not.

## Advertising fixes — no output change

| fix | affected |
|---|---|
| `CONSTRUCTS` declared wherever `CALLS` is — it is relabelled off the *same* pass when the callee resolves to a type | 16 languages, declared for none |
| Julia and R added to `supportsCallExtraction` — both have grammars, both resolve calls (pinned by existing tests at `provider_test.go:12195` and `:12307`), yet capabilities reported them inventory-grade | 2 |
| Rust `OVERRIDES` for trait impls | 1 — **found by the new contract test, not by me** |
| Relation support declared for C, C++, Groovy, Julia, Kotlin, Ruby, Scala, Swift, Zig | 25 relations |

Zig advertised `CALLS/CONTAINS/DEFINES` while emitting `DATA_FLOWS`, `PARAM_TYPE`, `READS_FIELD` and `USES_TYPE`. AGENTS.md tells agents to feature-detect here, so this told them to skip a working graph.

## Behavior fixes

**Fast profile.** It skipped the entire per-symbol relation pass for 22 of 30 call-capable languages, so `search`'s default profile returned almost no call graph for Rust, C++, Kotlin, Swift, Scala, Zig and more — while both capability matrices advertised `CALLS`. Cargo measured **21,509 CALLS at `--profile full` against 14 at `--profile fast`**. Now an opt-out keyed on semantic support; the expensive C/C++ call scan keeps its existing separate opt-out, which is where the original benchmark pressure was (`55f24ae`).

**Return and parameter types from the parse tree.** The signature split anchors on the first `(` — the receiver for a Go method — and guesses unlisted languages' return type as the second-to-last word before it, i.e. the declaration keyword:

```
Swift  func f(a: Int) -> Result   ->  RETURNS_TYPE = [func]
Zig    fn f(a: u8) Result         ->  RETURNS_TYPE = [fn]
Scala  def f(a: Int): Result      ->  RETURNS_TYPE = [def]
Go     func (r *R) B(i In) Out    ->  PARAM from the RECEIVER; method name
                                      and param type read as return types
```

Zig had **zero** `RETURNS_TYPE` edges in an entire repository; it now has 1,036. Threaded as private fields (`Entity` → `SymbolRecord` → search cache), so schema 1.x and `compound-v1` IDs are untouched.

**GraphQL scan precision.** The body scan ran on every language with `(query|mutation|subscription) <word>`, case-insensitive — matching prose. It emitted **1,245 edges in cli-cli and 1,057 in spring-framework** with targets like `query the`. Now restricted to the languages that declare `HANDLES_GRAPHQL`, which is what capabilities already promised. Python (88) and TypeScript (17) edges are preserved; the precise `graphql_resolver`/`graphql_schema_field` branches stay ungated.

## Structural

- `importsFor` and `importCapableExtension` were parallel switches a comment asked editors to keep mirrored by hand; both now read one registry, which also hoists per-file regex compilation to package scope.
- `docs/baseline-report.md` called `HANDLES_GRPC`/`GRAPHQL`/`TRPC`/`CONFIGURES` globally heuristic while all four are attributed per language.

## Guards

- `TestCapabilityMatrixCoversEmittedRelations` — every relation a fixture emits must be declared per-language or as a global heuristic. **One direction only**: a fixture lacking a construct is not evidence of missing capability.
- Fixture coverage raised from 11 to 21 languages (`julia-r-basic`, `multilang-relations`), because the guard only sees languages that appear in a fixture — and the fixtures covered none of the languages the matrix was wrong about. Adding them surfaced the 25 undeclared relations above, independently matching the corpus measurement.
- `TestImportCapabilityMatchesScannerRegistry`, `TestHeuristicRelationTypesMatchDocumentation`, `TestASTSignatureTypes*` (9 grammars + the keyword-return regression).

## Verification

| check | result |
|---|---|
| P0 + registry output impact | **byte-identical** across all 12 corpus/profile snapshots |
| full suite, gofmt, vet | green |
| snapshot determinism | 5 runs, one hash |
| cached vs cold `--head` | identical content |
| fast `CALLS` ⊆ full `CALLS` | **0** spurious edges across 4 repos |

Aggregate deltas — `full`: RETURNS_TYPE **+2,893**, HANDLES_GRAPHQL **−2,327**, PARAM_TYPE **−1,403**, CALLS +150. `fast`: CALLS **+10,539**, CONSTRUCTS +381.

Every category of removal was opened against source. `PARAM_TYPE` losses were parameter *names* (`args`, `run`) and receivers; `RETURNS_TYPE` losses were parameter types or the method's own name — `CommandStubber.Register -> CommandCallback` on a method that returns nothing, `load_host_triple -> GlobalContext` where that is a parameter. Gains verified too: Zig's `reclaim_table(...) ?*RepairTable` now correctly yields `RepairTable`.

## Two things to weigh before merging

**The fast profile is slower** where it now does work it previously skipped (median of 3, post-warmup):

| repo | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| cargo | 4.27s | 10.41s |
| pandas | 41.99s | 71.34s |
| spring | 26.86s | 30.79s |
| cli-cli | 10.98s | 9.32s |

Cargo at `fast` is still 3.6× faster than at `full` (37.85s) while going from 14 CALLS to 8,914. My judgement is that the old behavior wasn't fast, it was empty — but this is the reversible part of the PR if you disagree.

**The GraphQL gate is incomplete.** It aligns emission with declared capability but does not tighten the pattern *within* declaring languages: pandas retains 88 edges named `query the`, `query is`, `query that`. That is a precision fix outside this plan's scope; happy to follow up.

Unrelated pre-existing issue noticed, not touched: `self-assignment of i to i` at `internal/cli/search.go:1193` (from `bd325aa` on the base branch) trips `go vet ./internal/...`.

content.text:
Here's the answer to your question, with the benchmark still confirming the end-to-end numbers.

## The regression was mostly not my change — it was pre-existing waste my change switched on

I profiled instead of guessing. On a cargo fast-profile snapshot:

| cost | share |
|---|---|
| `syscall.Lstat` | 36% of the run |
| `resolvedJavaScriptReexportTargets` | **32%** |
| regex *matching* | ~25% |
| regex *compilation* | 0.15% (not a factor) |

**`resolvedJavaScriptReexportTargets` had no language gate.** For every resolved import in *any* language it opened the target file and scanned it for `export { x } from "./y"` syntax, recursing up to eight levels. A Rust `use` target cannot contain JavaScript, so a third of the run was spent looking for JS in Rust files — and each of those file opens is where the `Lstat` time came from too.

That inefficiency predates my work. It just never mattered before, because the fast profile skipped the per-symbol phase for 22 languages — the very skip I removed. So enabling the phase exposed a latent cost rather than creating one.

## The fix

Gate both re-export entry points on the target's extension (`.js/.jsx/.ts/.tsx/.mjs/.cjs/.mts/.cts`). Nine lines plus a helper.

**In-process benchmark: 7.05s → 3.82s, a 46% cut.**

**Output is unchanged** — all 12 corpus/profile snapshots byte-identical, including vite where the chain still runs. A TypeScript fixture confirms `run -> compute` still resolves through `export { compute } from "./impl"` with `resolution=import_resolved`. Full suite, gofmt, vet green.

Committed as `7e4adbc` (not yet pushed).

## What's left if you want more

Two further levers I found but didn't pull, since this one alone likely covers most of the gap:

1. **The double read.** Each file is read once in the parse phase and again in the relation phase, and the `read` closure does an `os.Lstat` per call. Caching the Lstat verdict (path → regular/size) would halve those stats without holding content, preserving the memory-bounded streaming design.
2. **Targeted opt-outs**, per Codex's original advice — keep the generic fast path but exempt specific languages where a benchmark proves the cost isn't worth it.

I'll post the final base-vs-after timings when the three-way benchmark lands. If the residual gap is small, I'd stop here; if cargo is still meaningfully above baseline, the Lstat cache is the next cheapest win.

The three-way results are in, and they force me to correct something I told you earlier.

| repo (fast) | base | before perf fix | after perf fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| cargo | 3.40s | 8.29s | **4.42s** |
| cli-cli | 6.20s | 6.17s | 5.48s |
| spring | 22.87s | 23.49s | 24.64s |
| pandas | 40.19s | 32.98s | 40.57s |

**Cargo is the real signal:** 8.29s → 4.42s recovers about 80% of the regression, leaving ~1.3× over baseline instead of 2.4×. That's corroborated by the in-process benchmark (7.05s → 3.82s), which has no process-startup noise.

**But the other three rows are noise, and that means my earlier numbers were too.** Look at pandas: 32.98s *before* the perf fix, which is faster than the 40.19s baseline — impossible, since that change only adds work. And spring reads as slower *after* a change that only removes work. This machine has been swinging ±40% on the large repos across runs; I've measured spring at 62.42s, 35.20s, 26.86s and 22.87s for the same binary.

So the figure I reported earlier — "pandas 41.99 → 71.34s, 1.7× slower" — is not trustworthy. I presented it as a measurement when it was within the noise band. The honest position is that cargo is the only repo where the regression exceeds measurement error on this hardware, and that's the one the fix addresses.

I've launched a 5-repetition run reporting min/median/max for pandas and cargo, so the spread is visible rather than hidden behind a median. That will settle whether any pandas regression exists at all.

toolUseResult.originalFile:
Stacked on #75 (base: `claude/tree-sitter-parameter-names`). Draft.

Third in the chain from the determinism report in #73. #75 fixed one instance of a defect class; this fixes the class wherever it appears, and adds the guards that make it stay fixed.

**The class:** a capability is gated on a hand-maintained per-language list while the real behavior is generic, so the two drift — and a language silently gets a worse path, or a promise the provider does not keep.

The codebase already had the right pattern in the same file: `supportsSemanticExtraction` derives from `spec.grammar != nil`, and `importCapable` derives from a shared predicate. `supportsCallExtraction` (a 30-language switch) and `ooRelationSupport` (a hand table) did not.

## Advertising fixes — no output change

| fix | affected |
|---|---|
| `CONSTRUCTS` declared wherever `CALLS` is — it is relabelled off the *same* pass when the callee resolves to a type | 16 languages, declared for none |
| Julia and R added to `supportsCallExtraction` — both have grammars, both resolve calls (pinned by existing tests at `provider_test.go:12195` and `:12307`), yet capabilities reported them inventory-grade | 2 |
| Rust `OVERRIDES` for trait impls | 1 — **found by the new contract test, not by me** |
| Relation support declared for C, C++, Groovy, Julia, Kotlin, Ruby, Scala, Swift, Zig | 25 relations |

Zig advertised `CALLS/CONTAINS/DEFINES` while emitting `DATA_FLOWS`, `PARAM_TYPE`, `READS_FIELD` and `USES_TYPE`. AGENTS.md tells agents to feature-detect here, so this told them to skip a working graph.

## Behavior fixes

**Fast profile.** It skipped the entire per-symbol relation pass for 22 of 30 call-capable languages, so `search`'s default profile returned almost no call graph for Rust, C++, Kotlin, Swift, Scala, Zig and more — while both capability matrices advertised `CALLS`. Cargo measured **21,509 CALLS at `--profile full` against 14 at `--profile fast`**. Now an opt-out keyed on semantic support; the expensive C/C++ call scan keeps its existing separate opt-out, which is where the original benchmark pressure was (`55f24ae`).

**Return and parameter types from the parse tree.** The signature split anchors on the first `(` — the receiver for a Go method — and guesses unlisted languages' return type as the second-to-last word before it, i.e. the declaration keyword:

```
Swift  func f(a: Int) -> Result   ->  RETURNS_TYPE = [func]
Zig    fn f(a: u8) Result         ->  RETURNS_TYPE = [fn]
Scala  def f(a: Int): Result      ->  RETURNS_TYPE = [def]
Go     func (r *R) B(i In) Out    ->  PARAM from the RECEIVER; method name
                                      and param type read as return types
```

Zig had **zero** `RETURNS_TYPE` edges in an entire repository; it now has 1,036. Threaded as private fields (`Entity` → `SymbolRecord` → search cache), so schema 1.x and `compound-v1` IDs are untouched.

**GraphQL scan precision.** The body scan ran on every language with `(query|mutation|subscription) <word>`, case-insensitive — matching prose. It emitted **1,245 edges in cli-cli and 1,057 in spring-framework** with targets like `query the`. Now restricted to the languages that declare `HANDLES_GRAPHQL`, which is what capabilities already promised. Python (88) and TypeScript (17) edges are preserved; the precise `graphql_resolver`/`graphql_schema_field` branches stay ungated.

## Structural

- `importsFor` and `importCapableExtension` were parallel switches a comment asked editors to keep mirrored by hand; both now read one registry, which also hoists per-file regex compilation to package scope.
- `docs/baseline-report.md` called `HANDLES_GRPC`/`GRAPHQL`/`TRPC`/`CONFIGURES` globally heuristic while all four are attributed per language.

## Guards

- `TestCapabilityMatrixCoversEmittedRelations` — every relation a fixture emits must be declared per-language or as a global heuristic. **One direction only**: a fixture lacking a construct is not evidence of missing capability.
- Fixture coverage raised from 11 to 21 languages (`julia-r-basic`, `multilang-relations`), because the guard only sees languages that appear in a fixture — and the fixtures covered none of the languages the matrix was wrong about. Adding them surfaced the 25 undeclared relations above, independently matching the corpus measurement.
- `TestImportCapabilityMatchesScannerRegistry`, `TestHeuristicRelationTypesMatchDocumentation`, `TestASTSignatureTypes*` (9 grammars + the keyword-return regression).

## Verification

| check | result |
|---|---|
| P0 + registry output impact | **byte-identical** across all 12 corpus/profile snapshots |
| full suite, gofmt, vet | green |
| snapshot determinism | 5 runs, one hash |
| cached vs cold `--head` | identical content |
| fast `CALLS` ⊆ full `CALLS` | **0** spurious edges across 4 repos |

Aggregate deltas — `full`: RETURNS_TYPE **+2,893**, HANDLES_GRAPHQL **−2,327**, PARAM_TYPE **−1,403**, CALLS +150. `fast`: CALLS **+10,539**, CONSTRUCTS +381.

Every category of removal was opened against source. `PARAM_TYPE` losses were parameter *names* (`args`, `run`) and receivers; `RETURNS_TYPE` losses were parameter types or the method's own name — `CommandStubber.Register -> CommandCallback` on a method that returns nothing, `load_host_triple -> GlobalContext` where that is a parameter. Gains verified too: Zig's `reclaim_table(...) ?*RepairTable` now correctly yields `RepairTable`.

## Two things to weigh before merging

**The fast profile is slower** where it now does work it previously skipped (median of 3, post-warmup):

| repo | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| cargo | 4.27s | 10.41s |
| pandas | 41.99s | 71.34s |
| spring | 26.86s | 30.79s |
| cli-cli | 10.98s | 9.32s |

Cargo at `fast` is still 3.6× faster than at `full` (37.85s) while going from 14 CALLS to 8,914. My judgement is that the old behavior wasn't fast, it was empty — but this is the reversible part of the PR if you disagree.

**The GraphQL gate is incomplete.** It aligns emission with declared capability but does not tighten the pattern *within* declaring languages: pandas retains 88 edges named `query the`, `query is`, `query that`. That is a precision fix outside this plan's scope; happy to follow up.

Unrelated pre-existing issue noticed, not touched: `self-assignment of i to i` at `internal/cli/search.go:1193` (from `bd325aa` on the base branch) trips `go vet ./internal/...`.

Repo: /Users/thomi/Projects/entire-graph (Go, tree-sitter code-graph provider).
Branch claude/language-capability-generalization (PR #76). Three loose ends. For each I have a
proposed fix; tell me if you disagree, and propose better. Be concrete and push back.

Constraints: schema 1.x frozen/additive-only; provider is no-egress; compound-v1 symbol IDs stable.

=== ISSUE 1: GraphQL body scans are imprecise in ALL languages ===
Two regexes in internal/sem/types.go scan symbol BODIES:
  graphqlOperationRe          = `(?is)\b(query|mutation|subscription)\s+([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)`
  graphqlOperationSelectionRe = `(?is)\b(query|mutation|subscription)\b\s*(ident)?\s*(\([^{}]*\))?\s*(@dir)*\{`
I already gated both to the languages that DECLARE HANDLES_GRAPHQL (TS/JS/Python/GraphQL), which
removed 2,327 undeclared edges from Go/Java. What remains is a precision problem INSIDE the
declaring languages. Measured across 6 real repos (evidence kind -> count, example target):
  cli-cli   Go     graphql_operation        960  'query string'
  cli-cli   Go     graphql_operation_field  285  'query Name'
  spring    Java   graphql_operation        512  'query proxy'
  spring    Java   graphql_operation_field  545  'subscription cancel'   <-- a Java method decl
                                                                             `subscription cancel() {`
  pandas    Python graphql_operation         88  'query the'
  vite      TS     graphql_operation         17  'query string'
  tigerbeetle mixed graphql_operation/field  30
I believe ALL ~2,400 are false positives; none of these repos use GraphQL. Note the "precise"
selection-set regex is ALSO fooled: `subscription cancel() {` in Java, and it fires 843 times.
The repo's real GraphQL detection has separate, precise paths that I did NOT touch and that ARE
test-covered: symbol kinds graphql_resolver and graphql_schema_field (see parser_test.go,
typescript_test.go, testdata/fixtures/services-config).
MY PROPOSAL: require the operation text to be in an actual GraphQL context rather than anywhere in
a body — i.e. inside a template/string literal (gql`...`, graphql`...`, or a quoted string), or in
a .graphql/.gql file — and keep the selection-set requirement. Possibly delete graphqlOperationRe
(the no-`{` variant) entirely since a GraphQL operation always has a selection set.
QUESTIONS: (a) is deleting the no-brace variant safe, or does it catch a real shape I'd lose?
(b) is "must be inside a string/template literal" the right precision signal for TS/JS/Python?
(c) should this ship in PR #76 or separately, given it deletes ~2,400 edges?

=== ISSUE 2: os.Lstat is 23% of a fast-profile run ===
internal/sem/provider.go openSource() worktree reader:
    read := func(path string) (string, bool) {
        full := filepath.Join(repo, filepath.FromSlash(path))
        info, err := os.Lstat(full)                      // reject symlink, enforce size cap
        if err != nil || info.Mode()&fs.ModeSymlink != 0 || !info.Mode().IsRegular() { return "",false }
        if maxReadBytes > 0 && info.Size() > maxReadBytes { registry.note(...); return "", false }
        content, err := os.ReadFile(full)
        ...
Profile of a cargo fast snapshot (4.22s total, AFTER I fixed a separate 32% JS-scan waste):
  syscall.syscall 1.28s (30.9%); of that syscall.Lstat 0.96s = 23% of the whole run
  the read closure is 1.23s cum, 76% of which is os.Lstat
  callers: StreamSnapshot (parse phase) 0.52s, forEachRelation (relation phase) 0.46s,
           buildManifestImportResolver 0.20s  -> i.e. each file is read from ~2 phases
  by contrast syscall.Open is only 0.23s and Fstat 0.01s
MY PROPOSAL (preferred): stop calling Lstat at all. Use os.OpenFile(full, O_RDONLY|O_NOFOLLOW, 0),
then f.Stat() on the handle for mode+size, then read. O_NOFOLLOW makes open fail on a symlink
(ELOOP), preserving the symlink rejection; fstat on an open handle is ~free (0.01s measured); and
it removes the duplicate path walk entirely. This beats a stat cache because there is no
invalidation surface and no memory growth.
ALTERNATIVE: memoize path -> (ok,size) across phases.
QUESTIONS: (a) any portability/semantic trap with O_NOFOLLOW on macOS/Linux here? (b) does
anything depend on Lstat NOT opening the file (permissions, fifos, /dev nodes that block on open)?
That last one worries me: opening a fifo can block forever where Lstat would not.

## Issue 1 — split the fix

### (a) Delete the no-brace regex?

Delete `graphqlOperationRe`, yes. Delete the named-operation edge, no.

Every explicit GraphQL operation must have a selection set. However, GraphQL also has query shorthand—`{ viewer }`—which omits both `query` and the operation name. [The GraphQL grammar confirms both points.](https://spec.graphql.org/September2025/)

The current test explicitly preserves `query GetViewer` as a compatibility edge at [provider_test.go:8126](/Users/thomi/Projects/entire-graph/internal/sem/provider_test.go:8126). Derive that edge from the same validated operation that yields `query viewer`; do not independently substring-match the name.

Also add shorthand support. The test called “anonymous” currently uses `query { ... }`, not actual shorthand.

### (b) Require a string/template literal?

Necessary, but insufficient. “Anywhere inside any string” still catches documentation, code samples, snapshots, and test prose.

I recommend:

- First identify host-language AST literal nodes—JS/TS strings and templates, Python strings including triple-quoted strings.
- Validate the complete literal as a GraphQL executable document, rather than finding a GraphQL-looking substring.
- Emit named-operation and root-field edges from that one parse.
- Treat `gql`/`graphql` tags as strong context, but not mandatory: ordinary strings are used in `fetch` bodies and Python clients.
- Support `.graphql` and the already-supported `.graphqls`; add `.gql`, which is currently absent from [inventory_languages.go:56](/Users/thomi/Projects/entire-graph/internal/sem/inventory_languages.go:56).
- Attribute each literal to the smallest enclosing symbol by byte range.

That removes comments and method declarations structurally and handles variables, directives, aliases, fragments, multiple operations, and shorthand deliberately.

One more pushback: [serviceBoundaryScanLanguage](/Users/thomi/Projects/entire-graph/internal/sem/types.go:376) duplicates `ooRelationSupport`, which cuts against this PR’s generalization goal. Gate using `languageSupportsRelation(symbol.Language, "HANDLES_GRAPHQL")` so there is one source of truth.

### (c) PR #76 or separate?

Split it:

- Keep the undeclared-language gate in #76. That is directly necessary for truthful capability reporting and accounts for roughly 2,300 of the deleted edges.
- Put the host-literal/GraphQL-document extractor in a follow-up precision PR. It risks losing true supported-language edges and deserves positive-corpus testing.

So “deletes ~2,400 edges” conflates two changes with different risk profiles.

## Issue 2 — use open/fstat, but harden it

Your performance direction is right. `O_NOFOLLOW` on Linux and macOS rejects a final-component symlink, and `f.Stat()` examines the object actually opened, eliminating the current Lstat→ReadFile race. It follows intermediate symlinks, just as the current final-path `Lstat` effectively does. [Linux `open(2)`](https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/open.2.html) and [Apple `open(2)`](https://developer.apple.com/library/archive/documentation/System/Conceptual/ManPages_iPhoneOS/man2/open.2.html) document those semantics.

But I would not implement the proposal literally:

- `syscall.O_NOFOLLOW` is unavailable on Windows, while CI builds/tests Windows. Put the optimized helper behind `darwin || linux` build tags and retain the current Lstat path elsewhere.
- Add `O_NONBLOCK`. Otherwise a regular file replaced by a FIFO after enumeration can block forever. `O_NONBLOCK` has no meaningful effect on regular-file reads.
- A device node can still have effects merely from opening. Enumeration already rejects non-regular files at [provider.go:9899](/Users/thomi/Projects/entire-graph/internal/sem/provider.go:9899), so this requires a concurrent replacement race; `O_NONBLOCK` mitigates blocking but is not an absolute “never open devices” guarantee.
- Preserve oversized-unreadable behavior. Today Lstat can register an oversized file even when opening it would fail. On an open error, do a rare-path Lstat and register it if it is regular, non-symlink, and oversized.
- Use the helper for both `read` and `readPrefix`.
- Also use it in `oversizeRegistry.lookup`: [provider.go:9664](/Users/thomi/Projects/entire-graph/internal/sem/provider.go:9664) currently reopens through `filedigest.File`, which follows symlinks and can block if the path changes. Open safely, then call `filedigest.Stream`.
- Expect less than the full 23% improvement: `worktreeSourceFiles` still performs one necessary Lstat per listed file. You are removing repeated per-phase Lstats.

I prefer this over memoization. Ship it as a separate performance PR with symlink, FIFO, oversized-permission, Windows-build, and profile regression tests.

The premise is stale in the local refs:

- `origin/main` already contains `bd325aa`.
- `origin/main` also already has `flags.FileOutline = true`, introduced during merge commit `a50b9a4`.
- This branch is 5 commits behind and 8 ahead of `origin/main`.

Rebase or merge current `origin/main`. That resolves this exact vet failure without adding an unrelated commit to #76. The specific line should not conflict; if you add the same one-liner first, it will most likely become an empty patch during rebase rather than create a substantive conflict.

If restacking is temporarily impossible and branch-tip vet must pass immediately, the one-liner is safe—but treat it as disposable.

1. In #76, replace the duplicated GraphQL language allowlist with the capability lookup and retain negative Go/Java regression coverage.
2. Follow with an AST-literal plus validated-GraphQL-document extractor; retain named-operation edges and add shorthand and `.gql`.
3. Land the no-follow/nonblocking open helper as an independent performance PR.
4. Rebase #76 onto `origin/main`; do not add the vet-only commit.

Every explicit GraphQL operation must have a selection set. However, GraphQL also has query shorthand—`{ viewer }`—which omits both `query` and the operation name. [The GraphQL grammar confirms both points.](https://spec.graphql.org/September2025/)

### (b) Require a string/template literal?

Necessary, but insufficient. “Anywhere inside any string” still catches documentation, code samples, snapshots, and test prose.

## Issue 3 — vet: Codex talked me *out* of my fix

I was going to apply main's one-liner. Codex disagreed, and the evidence backs it: main already has `flags.FileOutline = true` (via merge `a50b9a4`), and my branch is **5 behind / 8 ahead** of main. The right resolution is restacking, not adding a duplicate commit that becomes an empty patch on rebase. **Nothing committed** — this is now a note that the stack needs updating, not a fix.

## Issue 2 — read path: Codex caught a CI break

My `O_NOFOLLOW` proposal would have **broken the Windows build** — CI runs `go build ./...` and `go test ./...` on `windows-latest`, and `syscall.O_NOFOLLOW` is undefined there (verified: `undefined: syscall.O_NOFOLLOW`). Implemented per its guidance:

- Fast path behind `//go:build darwin || linux`; portable file keeps `Lstat`-then-open. All three GOOS values verified to compile.
- `O_NONBLOCK` added so a path that became a FIFO can't hang the snapshot.
- `noteUnreadableOversize` preserves a record I'd have silently dropped — the old `Lstat`-first reader registered oversized files even when opening failed.
- Tests: symlink refused, FIFO neither blocks nor passes as regular, unreadable-oversize still registered.

Output byte-identical on cargo fast and tigerbeetle full. Committed as `90d181d` on its own branch, per Codex's advice to keep it out of #76.

## Issue 1 — GraphQL: split, and Codex found a flaw in my own fix

It pointed out that my `serviceBoundaryScanLanguage` **duplicated `ooRelationSupport`** — a second copy of "who supports HANDLES_GRAPHQL", which is exactly the drift this PR set exists to eliminate. Fair hit. It now reads `languageSupportsRelation(...)`, with tests asserting gate and table agree. Committed to #76 as `c51f992`.

The precision work is a follow-up, and Codex sharpened it beyond my plan: derive the named-operation edge from the *same validated operation* rather than substring-matching, support GraphQL query shorthand (`{ viewer }`), parse the host-language literal as a GraphQL document rather than requiring "inside any string" (which still catches docs and test prose), and add `.gql` to the inventory languages.

I'm waiting on the read-path benchmark. Note Codex's caveat: expect **less than** the 23%, since `worktreeSourceFiles` still does one necessary `Lstat` per file — this removes the repeated per-phase ones.

Want me to build that GraphQL document extractor next, or park it as an issue?

content.text:
The read-path work is reverted and the branch deleted (never pushed). Here's the honest outcome of all three.

## Issue 2 — implemented, measured, discarded

I built exactly what Codex and I agreed on: `O_NOFOLLOW|O_NONBLOCK` + fstat behind `darwin || linux` tags, Windows fallback, oversize-record preservation, tests for symlink/FIFO/oversize. All of it worked and output was byte-identical.

**It just didn't make anything faster.** Two independent 5-run benchmarks, including after I found and fixed a genuine defect in my own code (`io.ReadAll` instead of a pre-sized buffer). Cargo median 5.00 → 4.91, pandas 38.87 → 38.32; ranges overlap.

The profile's "Lstat = 23% of the run" did not translate into a 23% saving, because that time isn't the syscall — it's the kernel resolving the path. Drop `Lstat` and `open` pays it instead. Net zero. That's the lesson: a profile tells you where time is *attributed*, not what removing the call will *save*.

So it shipped nothing. It would have added a platform build-tag split, a hand-rolled read loop replacing `os.ReadFile`, and a subtle oversize fallback — for a benefit I'd disproven. The TOCTOU hardening it also provided is real, but that wasn't the motivation, and I'm not going to smuggle complexity in under a performance claim I've retracted.

**The remaining ~20% cargo cost is genuine work** — actually scanning Rust symbols — not overhead I can optimise away.

## Where the three landed

| issue | outcome |
|---|---|
| GraphQL gate duplication | **Fixed**, in #76 (`c51f992`) — gate reads `languageSupportsRelation`, tests assert it can't diverge from the table |
| GraphQL precision | Scoped as a follow-up, with Codex's refinements (validated-document parse, query shorthand, `.gql`) |
| Lstat / read path | **Closed as not worth doing** — built, measured, reverted |
| vet self-assignment | **Closed by not fixing** — main already has it; the stack needs restacking |

Codex changed my mind on two of the three, and caught a Windows CI break in the third before I shipped it.

Current state: on `claude/language-capability-generalization`, clean, one unpushed commit (`c51f992`). PR #76 is otherwise up to date. Want me to push that commit, and shall I open issues for the two deferred items — the GraphQL document extractor and the stack rebase?

content.text:
Done — the GraphQL precision fix was the substance I'd deferred, and it's now implemented rather than filed.

**PR #76** (https://github.com/entireio/entire-graph/pull/76) — two more commits pushed, body updated so the old "incomplete" caveat now reads as fixed.

| repo | false positives before | after |
|---|---|---|
| pandas | 88 | **0** |
| vite | 17 | **0** |
| tigerbeetle | 5 | **0** |

The fix rests on one observation: a GraphQL document is always embedded as a *literal* — a `gql\`\`` template, a string handed to a client, a Python triple-quoted block — never as bare code. Scanning literals only removes the code and comment cases structurally; requiring a selection set inside the literal removes the prose. And the named-operation edge is now derived from a validated operation instead of an independent substring match, per Codex.

Critically, I verified it still finds *real* GraphQL rather than just finding nothing — all three embedding shapes resolve, and a class method `query() { … }` (the false positive Codex predicted) now yields nothing. The corpus delta is only `HANDLES_GRAPHQL` edges, the `external:graphql:*` nodes they were the sole reference to, and summary counts.

## Final state of the three

| issue | outcome |
|---|---|
| GraphQL | **Fixed** — gate dedup + literal-context precision, 110 false positives gone |

content.text:
All three done and pushed to **PR #76** (now 7 commits).

**The `mutation $id` bug** turned out to be a one-character omission worth understanding: the root-field scanner leaves its cursor just past a field name, and the loop's `i++` then skips the next byte. When that byte is the `(` of an argument list, the depth counter never rises — so `id: $id` gets read at depth 0, where `:` makes it look like an alias and yields a field named `$id`. The alias branch already compensated with `i = cursor - 1`; the plain branch didn't. That also explains the shape-dependence that puzzled me: only argument-carrying root fields were affected.

**Query shorthand** now works, but deliberately only under a `gql`/`graphql` tag. Detecting bare `{ … }` strings as operations would have quietly undone the precision fix I'd just made — a JSON blob or object literal in a string would read as a query. Verified both ways: `gql\`{ viewer { id } }\`` produces `query viewer` and `query settings`; an untagged template and `"{ foo: 1, bar: 2 }"` produce nothing.

**`.gql`** registers as GraphQL, confirmed end-to-end.

One thing to be straight about: **these three move nothing in the corpora** — none of the six repos has a `.gql` file, uses shorthand, or had a surviving argument-carrying root field. So unlike the earlier work, they're carried by unit tests rather than measurement. I've said so in both the commit and the PR body rather than letting the absence of a number imply an absence of risk.

content.text:
Yes — and it was worth doing, because **it caught a regression my unit tests missed.**

I found real `.gql` files locally, including in this repo's own bench cache: NestJS GraphQL samples and a Tina-generated `queries.gql` from the next.js examples.

## What validation exposed

All 18 edges on the real tree came from `schema.gql` — **none** from `queries.gql`. My literal-context rule assumed GraphQL is always embedded in a host language, but in a `.graphql`/`.gql` file the whole file *is* the document, so there's no literal to look inside. Confirmed directly:

```
before my work:  query posts [graphql_operation]   +  query $relativePath  (the variable bug)
after (broken):  (none)
after (fixed):   query posts [graphql_operation]
```

I'd have shipped that. Unit tests didn't catch it because I wrote them all around embedded literals — the shape I had in mind.

## The before/after on real repos

| | before this change set | after |
|---|---|---|
| `.gql` files recognized | **0** | 4 |
| boundaries | 14, essentially all junk — `query is`, `mutation return`, `subscription return` scraped from TypeScript code and comments | 49, all from real `.gql` files |
| breakdown | — | 18 schema fields, 3 named operations, 28 operation root fields |
| variables as fields | `query $relativePath` | none |

The Tina file was a lucky draw: `query posts($relativePath: String!) { posts(relativePath: $relativePath) … }` is exactly the argument-carrying root field that triggered the off-by-one, so it validates that fix on real generated code rather than my synthetic fixture.

Host-language precision is untouched — pandas and vite remain at zero false positives.

Committed as `b3a98a0` and pushed to PR #76, with a regression test built from the real `queries.gql` shape so this specific gap can't reopen. Full suite, gofmt, vet green.

The honest lesson: I validated the earlier corpus work against six repos and caught real problems, then wrote these three fixes against fixtures I invented and declared them "carried by unit tests." That asymmetry is where the bug got in.

14	`internal/sem/golden_test.go` (`TestProviderGoldenSnapshots`) snapshots each

content.content:
═══ PR #75 ═══
── internal/sem/parameters.go:251
cleanParameterName currently rejects any non-ASCII identifier characters. Many supported languages allow Unicode identifiers (e.g., Go, Kotlin, Swift), so this can drop legitimate parameter names and silently suppress DATA_FLOWS matches for code that uses non-ASCII identifiers.

Consider allowing non-ASCII runes rather than returning "" for them (or validating with Unicode categories).

═══ PR #76 ═══
── internal/sem/golden_test.go:480
The condition `got == nil && len(got) != 0` can never be true (a nil slice always has len 0), so this check is dead code and won’t catch malformed scanner results.

── internal/sem/testdata/fixtures/multilang-relations/store.zig:9
This Zig fixture returns a `Session` type that is not defined in the Zig file, which causes type relations to resolve (name-only) against the Kotlin `Session` in the same fixture. That couples the fixture languages and makes the Zig type edges ambiguous and brittle.

── internal/sem/types.go:450
The comment implies `graphql.experimental` is a supported tag value, but `templateLiteralTag` currently returns only the final identifier segment before the backtick (so `graphql.experimental` becomes `experimental`). That’s fine behavior, but the comment is misleading as written.

── internal/sem/types.go:392
The comment says scanning only literals “removes the code and comment cases structurally”, but `hostLanguageLiterals` scans raw source text (including comments) and will still pick up quoted strings inside comments. That can still produce `HANDLES_GRAPHQL` edges for commented-out or example queries.

── internal/sem/types.go:504
`graphqlShorthandRootFields` claims to only accept documents that are “nothing but a selection set”, but it doesn’t verify that the closing brace is the end of the literal. Trailing content after the selection set would currently still be treated as shorthand and could create false positives.

`index` now defaults to `--format auto` (text when stdout is a terminal). Previously it always emitted JSON unless an invalid format was supplied, so this is a behavior change for any caller that parses `index` output from an interactive terminal. Build/warm the committed-tree cache before a batch of queries

Usage:
  entire graph index --repo . [--head] [--force] [--profile syntax-only|fast|full] [--cache-dir path] [--report GRAPH_REPORT.md] [--format text|json|auto]

Prebuilds the durable, query-independent committed-tree index so latency-sensitive --head searches/neighbors reuse it. Re-running index is also how you refresh a committed-tree cache: an unchanged tree hits, a changed tree rebuilds. Pass --force to rebuild and overwrite the entry even when the tree is unchanged.

At a terminal it draws a live progress bar on stderr (only when it actually builds — a cache hit returns instantly) and prints a readable summary; piped or with --format json it emits the schema-versioned JSON summary that agents and CI consume. --report writes a human-readable GRAPH_REPORT.md rendered from the snapshot, so the same tree always renders the same bytes. The cache defaults to the platform per-user cache dir (macOS ~/Library/Caches/entire-graph; XDG_CACHE_HOME or ~/.cache elsewhere); --cache-dir and ENTIRE_PLUGIN_DATA_DIR override it.

content.text:
Round 1 complete on all three, round 2 requested. **All 10 findings were legitimate** — I verified each rather than taking them on trust, and two were worse than reported.

## #75 — 1 finding

**Unicode identifiers rejected.** Copilot said this "can drop legitimate parameter names." Measuring it, `func f(café string, naïve int)` dropped **both** parameters — and because the list was still flagged AST-confirmed, the regex fallback never ran, so the function produced no data flows at all. Now rejects punctuation instead of non-ASCII.

## #76 — 5 findings

The sharpest: my Zig fixture returned a `Session` type it never defined, so the golden literally recorded `Zig:store.zig:function:connect → Kotlin:Session.kt:class:Session` — a cross-language edge baked into a test baseline. Defining the struct in the Zig file fixed it.

Also: a dead assertion (`got == nil && len(got) != 0` can never hold, so it checked nothing), shorthand not enforcing "nothing but a selection set," and two comments that overclaimed — including mine asserting literal-scanning removes comment cases "structurally." It doesn't: a commented-out operation with a selection set still matches. I corrected the claim and recorded why stripping comments was rejected (a `//` inside a URL would truncate the literal).

## #78 — 4 findings, 3 fixed

`isTerminal` accepted any character device, and `/dev/null` is one — so `index --format auto > /dev/null` printed a human summary to a caller who asked for no output. Verified the fix yields JSON. Plus a comment that was factually wrong (`help` *does* have a doc entry, so `help --help` is intercepted) and a usage line contradicting its own flag doc.

**I did not act on the fourth.** Copilot flags that defaulting `index` to `auto` changes behavior for machine consumers parsing output from a terminal. That's a deliberate design choice — it's what the PR is *for* — not a defect, so it's your call, and I said so in the commit rather than quietly changing your default.

Side effect worth flagging: fixing #75 required rebasing #76 onto it again, which conflicted in `parameters_test.go` (both branches append tests). I resolved it keeping both sets — 13 test functions, all passing.

Full suite, vet, and gofmt green on all three branches. I'll report round 2 when it lands.

content.text:
You're right to call it out. The automation had a concrete bug, not a hiccup.

## What was wrong

GitHub reports the same actor under **two different logins depending on the endpoint**:

- `/pulls/N/reviews` → `copilot-pull-request-reviewer[bot]`
- `/pulls/N/comments` → `Copilot`

My monitor polled `/reviews` filtering for `login=="Copilot"`. That predicate can never be true. It polled a permanently-false condition for 30 minutes and timed out silently — which is why you had to say "Hello?" to get the round-1 results, and why round 2 had **already landed 40 minutes earlier** while I sat waiting for it.

The new monitor matches `test("copilot"; "i")` against `/reviews`, compares against a recorded baseline count (2 → expect 3), and **prints an explicit TIMEOUT line with the counts** if it fails, so a silent non-fire can't happen again.

## Round 2, which I should have reported on my own

No new inline comments on any of the three — round 1 fully resolved. But the suppressed findings included a real functional gap:

**Go variadic forwarding was undetected.** `f(prefix string, args ...string)` calling `sink(args...)` emitted no forward flow, because Go declares the ellipsis *before* the type but writes it *after* the name at the call site, and matching is literal. Fixed — `args... -> sink()` now appears.

My first attempt at that fix broke Java: `String... c` attaches the ellipsis to the type and is called as plain `c`, so I was inventing a spelling no Java call site writes. Caught by the existing cross-grammar test; now gated on the ellipsis actually following the name.

Also fixed: an ASCII check evaluated *after* a `byte()` truncation (right answer, wrong order — it relied on a later condition to save it), and two comments that contradicted their own code — including one in #78 claiming a list excludes `help`/`version` when it ends with `"version", "help"`.

**Still your call on #78:** Copilot flags in round 2 that the PR *description* says there's no default/machine-output change, but `index` does now default to `auto`. That's a design decision plus a description inaccuracy, so I left both alone.

Round 3 requested on all three; the monitor now has a predicate that can actually match.
